name: DurableJobCoordinator

claim.precondition: host owns canonical data instance and is READY or explicitly allowed background-start state
claim.selection: select due queued/retry_wait job by deterministic ordering (next_attempt_at_utc NULL/earliest, created_at_utc, job_id)
claim.mutation: set state=running, claimed_run_id=current run_id, claim_started_at_utc=now, attempt_count=attempt_count+1, updated_at_utc=now
claim.commit: commit claim before external/file work begins

execute: run job-specific handler outside authoritative write transaction in background executor; handler may persist bounded checkpoints using short explicit transactions and must invoke owning-domain commands for accepted domain mutations

steps: reload exact job and verify claimed_run_id=current run_id and state=running
insert one job_attempts terminal row with ordinal=attempt_count
set durable_jobs state=completed, clear claim fields, update checkpoint/result technical state as contract permits
COMMIT
verify current claim
insert job_attempts row outcome=failed/cancelled
job-type retry policy classifies terminal failed vs retry_wait with explicit next_attempt_at_utc
clear claim fields and store bounded last_error_code
COMMIT
fail_or_retry.rule: retry schedule is technical workflow policy; it never fabricates domain lifecycle state

cancel.transaction: caller-owned UnitOfWork; no nested BEGIN/COMMIT and no Foundation command receipt
cancel.input: job_id + exact expected job_type/contract_version + owning-domain command_context
steps: load the exact durable_jobs row inside the caller UnitOfWork and require job_type/contract_version equal the caller expectation; mismatch or missing identity fails closed
if state=cancelled return ALREADY_CANCELLED without mutation
if state=completed or failed return TERMINAL_UNCHANGED without rewriting technical history

if state=running capture claimed_run_id, claim_started_at_utc and attempt_count, insert exactly one job_attempts row outcome=cancelled for that current ordinal, then set durable_jobs state=cancelled and clear claimed_run_id/claim_started_at_utc/next_attempt_at_utc
if state=queued, retry_wait or waiting_review set durable_jobs state=cancelled and clear next_attempt_at_utc/claim fields without inventing a job_attempts row for work that never held a running claim
set updated_at_utc=server-now and return DurableJobCancellationResultV1 to the owning-domain caller; caller decides whether to commit or roll the entire shared UnitOfWork back
rules: a revoked running handler loses coordinator authority immediately at commit; checkpoint/complete/fail must revalidate state+claim and reject the stale worker
an already-running handler may physically finish in-flight external CPU/file work, but that work cannot regain coordinator or owning-domain authority merely because it finishes
an optional in-process cancellation signal may be delivered only after commit as a latency optimization; correctness depends on persisted state/claim validation, never on that signal
the same owning-domain rollback that rejects cancellation also restores the prior durable job state/job-attempt history atomically

startup_recovery.precondition: new host already owns canonical data instance exclusively
steps: find state=running jobs whose claimed_run_id differs from current run
for each, in bounded transaction insert job_attempts outcome=interrupted using stored claim_started_at_utc and new recovery time
apply job-type recovery policy: queued, retry_wait, failed, or waiting_review
clear stale claim fields
never resume arbitrary in-memory code position; restart from durable checkpoint/contract

restore_reconciliation.precondition: a cryptographically and structurally verified historical database has replaced the live database, host remains QUIESCING, restored DB is open through the verified LLD-12 SQLCipher provider, and no coordinator claims are permitted yet
restore_reconciliation.transaction: one LLD-01 recovery-finalization UnitOfWork before runtime may become READY
steps: enumerate all restored durable_jobs in deterministic job_id order whose state is queued, running, waiting_review, or retry_wait

for a restored running row with a valid prior claimed_run_id/claim_started_at_utc, insert exactly one job_attempts row outcome=interrupted using that prior run identity and attempt_count ordinal if that ordinal is not already represented

set every restored nonterminal durable_jobs row to cancelled, clear claimed_run_id/claim_started_at_utc/next_attempt_at_utc, set last_error_code=RESTORE_SNAPSHOT_JOB_INVALIDATED, and preserve bounded payload/checkpoint only as historical technical evidence
leave completed, failed, and already-cancelled rows unchanged
commit this reconciliation in the same recovery-finalization boundary that records required restore receipt/audit evidence, before enabling ordinary job claims
rules: restoring a historical snapshot never silently replays queued/retry/waiting external work
no job-type opt-in restore-resume exists in Beta 1.0; an operator or owning-domain workflow must explicitly start genuinely desired new work after readiness
restored job cancellation is technical workflow reconciliation and does not reverse or fabricate owning-domain lifecycle state
unknown job type/version remains fail-closed and cannot become executable during restore

job_type_contract.registration: static application registry; unknown persisted job type/version is quarantined/failed-safe and not guessed

concurrency: one coordinator in one authoritative host; at most two background executor workers; a job may define a stronger per-source/per-type coalescing key in its owning LLD
shutdown: QUIESCING stops new claims; running handlers receive cooperative cancellation signal and either finish a safe checkpoint/terminal result or remain recoverable as prior-run interruption after process exit
